ModMetaData.name: Weazel Behavior Experiments
ModMetaData.author: ifchen0
ModMetaData.description:
Warning: this mod was written with AI coding tools (Claude Code).
Small experimental behaviours for the XCC faction of Weazel Mode.
These scenarios are my own take on how the Weazels would act, based on my impression of the faction. They are not part of the original mod's lore and are not endorsed by its author.
Protection racket While your colony is neutral with XCC, a trade caravan from a faction hostile to XCC may draw an XCC strike team onto your map. The team hunts the caravan, and once the caravan is gone (defeated or left) it carries off the caravan's downed people and grabs valuables lying nearby before leaving. XCC treats a neutral colony as its own turf, and deals in slaves.
Captives, not recruits In vanilla, kidnapped people join their kidnappers after about 30 days. XCC keeps the people it carries off captive instead, so your kidnapped colonists can still be ransomed back. After about 30 days a captive is also put up for sale, and an XCC slave merchant may bring them along (at most 2 per merchant; Ideology needed), stripped of weapons, everything they carry and any apparel worth 320 silver or more. A colonist you buy back rejoins as a colonist; anyone else you buy is your slave, and goes home to the faction XCC took them from if emancipated. Colonists nobody buys go back into captivity; anyone else is gone for good.
Wasted time An XCC squad called in with favor, or requested from an allied XCC on the comms console, that leaves without taking any damage takes silver from anywhere on your map before leaving, leaving other goods alone. They feel you wasted their time. A squad that did fight takes the weapons and apparel left lying outside your storage instead, as spoils of the fight. A squad that breaks and flees just runs.
Failed ceremony XCC blames you for any failed bestowing ceremony, whether you let it expire, a raid broke it up or someone died, and takes goodwill for it (15 by default). It never drops goodwill low enough to turn XCC hostile, since a war would break out with their officer still on your map.
Keeping relations good Left alone, a neutral XCC drifts towards war: every 50 days vanilla lowers its goodwill by 10. If XCC's goodwill is below 0 and your colony is worth at least 14,000 silver, XCC sends a 10-member squad to "keep relations good" instead. They walk in to where caravans unload, take silver from anywhere on the map and leave. The silver buys goodwill back as a vanilla gift would, and the squad takes no more than it needs to bring XCC up to 80, just past an alliance at 75. If they find no silver, the usual drop applies.
Notes - A strike team member carries off the most valuable load within a wide radius, your stockpiles included, or leaves empty-handed. Squads collecting from you take one stack of silver each. Strike teams leave closed rooms alone; a squad you called in knows its way around and opens your doors. - A message in the top-left corner appears when something touches you: a strike team arriving, a squad taking your silver, your people put up for sale (no letters). Looting a beaten caravan and collecting battlefield gear happen without one. - Attacking the team turns XCC hostile, as with any neutral visitor. - Safe to add to an existing save. Remove it only when no XCC strike team or collecting squad is on the map.
